Yes. The old test depended on `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT` from the environment, and the fixed one doesn't. I ran the old version and the fixed version of the test with the variable set to `2`, as it would be on a CI re-run.

I ran `squeal proof scripts/release-identity.test.mjs --base HEAD~1 --case test --env GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2`. That runs the test as it was at `6a0ff949` and as it is at `9408de7a`, over the same release code.

- **Old test (`6a0ff949`): fails.** The version it computes has the run attempt appended. The nightly and PR release tests both fail:
  - nightly: `1.2.3-nightly.20261108.9.2`, expected `1.2.3-nightly.20261108.9`
  - PR: `1.2.3-pr7.9.2`, expected `1.2.3-pr7.9`
- **Fixed test (`9408de7a`): passes.** With the same `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2` in the environment, it passes. Without that variable set, the old test also passes, so the failure depends only on the variable.

The cause is in how `run()` builds the child environment in `scripts/release-identity.test.mjs`. The old version stripped only `GITHUB_ACTIONS` from the inherited environment. `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT` therefore leaked through to `scripts/release-snapshot.mjs:62`, which reads it and adds it to the version when it is numeric. A first CI run has attempt `1`, which doesn't change the version. A re-run has attempt `2` or higher, which does.

The fixed version does two things:
- It strips every inherited `GITHUB_*` variable, with the filter `GITHUB_`.
- It sets `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT: '1'` explicitly in the child environment.

The test now gets the same attempt number whatever the CI runner provides.

The proof reports 1 proven, 0 not red, 0 red for another reason, 0 not green. The green run was executed by the command and isn't stored, because a run under an injected variable is never stored.
